name: University of Copenhagen
description: Denmark's oldest and largest university, ranked among Europe's leading research institutions with roughly 38,000 students across six faculties.

name: Aarhus University
description: Denmark's second-largest university, spanning five faculties with strong research programmes in health, natural sciences and business.

name: Technical University of Denmark
description: Denmark's leading technical university, founded at the initiative of Hans Christian Ørsted, specializing in engineering and natural science research.

name: University of Southern Denmark
description: A multi-campus university formed through the 1998 merger of Odense University with regional institutions, active in health, engineering and humanities research.

name: Aalborg University
description: Internationally recognized as the birthplace of problem-based learning (PBL), with campuses in Aalborg, Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

name: Copenhagen Business School
description: One of Europe's largest business schools, conducting research across economics, management and social sciences.

name: Roskilde University
description: Founded as a reform university built around interdisciplinary, project-organized research and teaching.

name: IT University of Copenhagen
description: Denmark's youngest university, dedicated to research and education in computer science, digital design and business IT.

name: Rigshospitalet (Copenhagen University Hospital)
description: Denmark's largest and most highly specialized hospital, serving as the national and Nordic referral centre for advanced treatment and clinical research.

name: Aarhus University Hospital
description: Denmark's second-largest hospital, formed by merging Aarhus Sygehus and Skejby Sygehus, and the main teaching hospital for Aarhus University.

name: Odense University Hospital
description: One of Denmark's four university hospitals, serving as the primary teaching and research hospital for the University of Southern Denmark.

name: Copenhagen University Hospital – Herlev and Gentofte
description: A merged Capital Region hospital combining Herlev's cancer and specialist treatment with Gentofte's acute and medical services, affiliated with the University of Copenhagen.

name: Aalborg University Hospital
description: North Denmark Region's largest hospital and university hospital, closely affiliated with Aalborg University's Faculty of Medicine.

name: Copenhagen University Hospital – Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg
description: A merged Copenhagen hospital known for research in emergency medicine, rheumatology and public health, teaching hospital for the University of Copenhagen.

name: Copenhagen University Hospital – Amager and Hvidovre
description: A merged Copenhagen hospital with research strengths in gastroenterology, imaging and reproductive medicine, teaching hospital for the University of Copenhagen.

name: Zealand University Hospital
description: Denmark's newest university hospital, created from the merger of Roskilde and Køge hospitals to serve as Region Zealand's main teaching and research hospital.

name: Steno Diabetes Center Copenhagen
description: A specialized diabetes treatment, research and education centre operated by the Capital Region of Denmark in partnership with the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

name: Steno Diabetes Center Aarhus
description: A diabetes research, treatment and prevention centre based on the Aarhus University Hospital campus, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

name: Statens Serum Institut
description: Denmark's national institute for infectious disease control, biopreparedness and diagnostics, operating under the Ministry of Health.

name: Niels Bohr Institute
description: A world-renowned physics research institute founded by Niels Bohr, now part of the University of Copenhagen's Faculty of Science.

name: Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters
description: Denmark's oldest learned society and national academy of sciences, administering major research prizes and international scholarly exchange.

name: Danish Meteorological Institute
description: Denmark's national meteorological and climate research agency, providing forecasting and research for Denmark, Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

name: Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland
description: Denmark's independent national institution for geological, hydrological and energy research, advising government on climate, water and mineral resources.

name: Alexandra Institute
description: A non-profit applied IT research institute working on digitalization, AI and data-driven innovation with businesses and the public sector.

name: Danish Technological Institute
description: An independent, non-profit applied research and technology institute serving Danish industry across manufacturing, robotics and food technology.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Research
description: A University of Copenhagen research centre studying human proteins and their role in disease, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Basic Metabolic Research
description: A University of Copenhagen research centre investigating the genetic and physiological basis of obesity, diabetes and related metabolic disease.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Stem Cell Medicine (reNEW)
description: An international stem cell research consortium spanning the University of Copenhagen, Leiden University Medical Center and the Murdoch Children's Research Institute.

name: Interdisciplinary Nanoscience Center
description: An Aarhus University research centre spanning chemistry, physics, biology and medicine to study materials and processes at the nanoscale.

name: DTU Space – National Space Institute
description: Denmark's national space research institute, working on satellite instrumentation, geodesy, remote sensing and astrophysics, part of DTU since 2008.

name: Danish Institute for International Studies
description: An independent government-funded think tank conducting research on foreign policy, security and international development.

name: VIVE – The Danish Center for Social Science Research
description: Denmark's national centre for applied social science and welfare research, formed by the merger of SFI and KORA.

name: Danish Institute for Advanced Study
description: An interdisciplinary elite research centre at the University of Southern Denmark, hosting cross-faculty research chairs.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Biosustainability
description: A DTU research centre developing biological production methods for chemicals, fuels and pharmaceuticals, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

name: National Institute of Public Health
description: Denmark's national public health research institute, part of the University of Southern Denmark since 2007, studying population health and disease prevention.

name: Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies
description: An Aarhus University institute for advanced study hosting international fellows for interdisciplinary, curiosity-driven research.

name: Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence
description: A Danish National Research Foundation centre of excellence based at the University of Copenhagen, conducting foundational research in artificial intelligence.

name: Rockwool Foundation Research Unit
description: An independent socioeconomic research unit within the Rockwool Foundation, studying welfare, labour markets and migration.

name: BioInnovation Institute
description: A non-profit life science incubator and research institute founded with funding from the Novo Nordisk Foundation to translate scientific discoveries into new ventures.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation
description: One of the world's largest philanthropic foundations, funding biomedical, biotechnology and sustainability research through grants to Danish and international institutions.

name: Lundbeck Foundation
description: A major Danish foundation funding biomedical and brain research, and the principal shareholder of the pharmaceutical company Lundbeck.

name: Carlsberg Foundation
description: Denmark's oldest major research foundation, established by brewer J.C. Jacobsen to fund natural sciences, humanities and social sciences research.

name: Villum Foundation
description: A private foundation established by VELUX founder Villum Kann Rasmussen, funding research in technical and natural sciences, climate and the environment.

name: Danish Cancer Society
description: Denmark's largest health charity, funding cancer research, prevention programmes and patient support, and operating its own research institute.

name: Danish National Research Foundation
description: An independent, government-established foundation funding long-term Centres of Excellence across all research fields in Denmark.
